socfpga_rst_mngr_ll.h

Reset Manager low-level driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

rstmgr_ll_assert
int32_t rstmgr_ll_assert(
uint32_t 
reg_address,
uint8_t 
bit_pos
)

Performs a direct Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) read-modify-write operation to set a specific bit within a Reset Manager register. Setting this bit actively drives the hardware reset line high for the associated peripheral, instantly halting its internal clocks, clearing its FIFOs, and freezing its state machines.

Parameters
reg_address
uint32_t

The absolute physical MMIO address of the target Reset Manager register.

bit_pos
uint8_t

The exact bit index (0-31) corresponding to the target peripheral's reset line.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code (such as -EINVAL) if the address is invalid or the bit position exceeds the 32-bit register width.

rstmgr_ll_deassert
int32_t rstmgr_ll_deassert(
uint32_t 
reg_address,
uint8_t 
bit_pos
)

Performs a direct MMIO read-modify-write operation to clear a specific bit within a Reset Manager register. Clearing this bit releases the hardware reset line, allowing the peripheral's internal logic to initialize and resume normal execution using the active system clock.

Parameters
reg_address
uint32_t

The absolute physical MMIO address of the target Reset Manager register.

bit_pos
uint8_t

The exact bit index (0-31) corresponding to the target peripheral's reset line.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code if the parameters are out of bounds.

rstmgr_ll_get_status
int32_t rstmgr_ll_get_status(
uint32_t 
reg_address,
uint8_t 
bit_pos,
uint8_t 
*
status
)

Samples the live, physical state of a specific Reset Manager register bit.  This bypasses higher-level software state tracking to provide the absolute hardware truth regarding whether a peripheral is currently being held in reset.

Parameters
reg_address
uint32_t

The absolute physical MMIO address of the target Reset Manager register.

bit_pos
uint8_t

The exact bit index (0-31) to sample.

status
uint8_t*

Pointer to an 8-bit variable where the masked state will be written (1 if the reset line is asserted, 0 if it is deasserted/active).

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the status pointer is NULL or parameters are invalid.
